title: Hardship Desk Guide — Good-Faith Days from Borrower Standing After a Returned Payment
content:
A deferral qualifying payment on Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts also carries a good-faith amount, applied to principal, equal to one day's interest on the principal balance at the contract APR over the tier's day-count basis multiplied by the good-faith days and rounded to the cent.

**The good-faith days start from the borrower's standing**, where an installment counts as paid when it was paid by a scheduled-installment payment that no returned payment reversed, and a returned payment counts when fewer than 12 whole months separate its date from the payment date:

| Installments paid | Returned payments in that 12-month window | Starting good-faith days |
|---|---|---|
| fewer than 12 | at least one | new-borrower good-faith days: 30 |
| 12 or more | at least one | seasoned-borrower good-faith days: 15 |
| any | none | no good-faith days |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- 11 installments paid, one return 4 whole months before the payment date: 30 days.
- 12 installments paid, the same return: 15 days.
- 40 installments paid, the only return 12 whole months before the payment date (for a payment on 2026-07-08, a return dated 2025-07-08): the return falls outside the window, so the borrower starts from no good-faith days. A return dated 2025-07-09 is 11 whole months back and counts: 15 days.

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

Principal balance 9800.00 at 15.59 percent over a 365-day basis gives one day's interest of 4.1858; 30 good-faith days give 125.57 and 15 give 62.79, each rounded once to the cent.
